title: Episode 243
source_name: AB Testing (formerly Modern Testing; Alan Page, Brent Jensen)
author: AB Testing
text: Hosts Alan Page (Spy) and Brent range across AI-assisted software development, the limits of automated testing, and how cascading failures happen in complex cloud systems. They then turn to voluntary retirement offers, financial certainty, purpose after work, and the challenge of making room for life beyond a demanding career.

title: [AINews] The No AI Slop Manifesto
author: swyx .ai
text: Congrats to both llama.ccp and ggml for reaching 1.0 (declaring stability and removing 35 deprecated functions from llama.cpp’s public header) and with SGLang also announcing 1.0 at the recent SGLang Summit . However, today’s title story goes to the No AI Slop manifesto , which arose out of the conference discussions at AIE CODE and which Dex introduced in the closing keynote after cosignatures by many of the speakers at the conference. It seems Hacker News also liked it , voting it up to the front page today. We started this manifesto to offer a useful tool for discussion at work, and hope it gets used that way. Georgi Gerganov · Daniel Han Chen’s example LangChain’s Series C. CapitalG led the round. LangSmith lets teams trace and evaluate production agents across frameworks. The company plans to announce new LangSmith features on November 20. LangChain · CapitalG Frontier and Open Model Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen in GitHub Copilot. GitHub made the model generally available in Copilot across its app, CLI and VS Code. GitHub Independent checks : Roboflow's vision bench shows high effort at 29.3s per image, against 51.4s for Argon and 132.3s for Carbon, though Carbon has better detection accuracy ( @skalskip92 ). One 3D-modeling test found Hydrogen more expensive than Argon because it loops on over-verification ( @dzhng ). Google's week : Google also shipped two 8th-gen TPUs, Gemini 4 Carbon, Gemini Robotics 2.5, AlphaGenome 2 and a Decisions API ( @sundarpichai ). MathArena : Gemini 4 Carbon took #1, displacing GPT-6.1 Sol ( @j_dekoninck ). Claude Fable 5.2 in Agent Arena. Arena published new results for long coding sessions. Pricing : API pricing fell from $10/$50 to $8/$40 per 1M input/output tokens ( @arena ). Agent Arena : The model ranks #1 at +30.4% net improvement, about 1.6x Opus 5.5. Its lead grows on long tasks, reaching 93% vs 85% no-correction responses at 16+ turns ( @arena , turns ). Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Small : The model's open weights are now on the Hub ( @ariG23498 ). It is the #1 US open model in Code Arena WebDev at 1647 ( @arena ). NVFP4 training : It uses a native 4-bit forward pass from the first pretraining step through the final RL rollout ( blog ). The mixed-precision recipe is detailed by @jackcookjack . NVFP4 is stored in 3.6x fewer bits than BF16 and runs up to 6x faster on GB300 ( quote ). Inference detail : A width-4 short convolution requires a rolling 3-token cache per layer alongside the KV cache ( @andrew_n_carr ). ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview (Baidu) : The model has 280B total and 14B active parameters, a 1M-token context and free OpenRouter access. Open weights are promised before Nov 25 ( @omarsar0 ), with Apache 2.0 cited by Arena. Other releases : Ripple-65B Preview : The dense model claims US open-weight SOTA on agentic coding ( @RicursiveAI ). title: Ask HN: What are the most useful, concrete AI skills to independently learn?
author: shnock
text: Specifically, what are the most useful, concrete skills to learn as an individual to take economic advantage of the advances in LLMs, agents and associated new technological capabilities? What is accessible to learn just from the internet and experimentation, without a degree program, assuming a preexisting moderately technical background? The clearer and more specific (eg. “Learn how-to x with y”) the better. Thank you!
